title: Eli Lilly Enters Psychedelic Drug Race With $3.8 Billion AtaiBeckley Acquisition
excerpt: The GLP-1 giant bets big on a psychedelic nasal spray for treatment-resistant depression, tapping into a market that could reach $12 billion by 2034.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Eli Lilly's acquisition of AtaiBeckley is valued at $3.8 billion, including milestone payments.
  • BPL-003, a nasal spray for depression, could generate $1-2 billion annually if successful.
  • The psychedelics market may reach $12 billion by 2034, rivaling current antidepressant sales.
  • AtaiBeckley was formed from a $390 million merger, highlighting its unique origins.

  • Eli Lilly will acquire AtaiBeckley for $2.8 billion upfront, with up to $1 billion more in milestone payments, totaling $3.8 billion.
  • The deal gives Lilly access to BPL-003, a psychedelic nasal spray in late-stage trials for treatment-resistant depression, with potential annual sales of $1-2 billion.
  • BPL-003 is a synthetic form of 5-MeO-DMT, a compound originally found in the Sonoran Desert toad.
  • The psychedelics industry could reach $12 billion in revenue by 2034, rivaling the size of branded antidepressants today.

Weight-Loss Profits Fund a New Frontier

Eli Lilly is leveraging its enormous weight-loss drug profits to make a bold move into one of medicine's most unconventional frontiers. The Indianapolis-based pharmaceutical giant announced it will acquire AtaiBeckley, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, in an all-cash deal valued at up to $3.8 billion.

Lilly will pay $6.75 per AtaiBeckley share upfront — a 26% premium to its closing price — plus contingent value rights worth up to $2.50 per share tied to clinical and regulatory milestones. AtaiBeckley shares surged more than 30% on the announcement.

The acquisition is the latest in a string of deals by Lilly, which has been on an aggressive buying spree fueled by windfall revenue from its GLP-1 obesity and diabetes franchise. Since early 2026, the company has struck deals for cancer biotech Kelonia Therapeutics, sleep-drug maker Centessa Pharmaceuticals, and three vaccine developers.

A Toad-Derived Compound Goes Clinical

At the heart of the deal is BPL-003, a synthetic form of 5-MeO-DMT — a psychedelic compound originally found in the secretions of the Sonoran Desert toad. Administered as a nasal spray, BPL-003 is in Phase 3 development for treatment-resistant depression, a severe form of the illness that fails to improve after standard treatments.

The theory behind psychedelic-based therapies is that they can restore neural plasticity in the brain, offering longer-lasting benefits while potentially reducing the burden of frequent medical visits that current treatments require.

AtaiBeckley expects initial results from its Phase 3 trials in early 2029. Jefferies analyst Andrew Tsai estimates BPL-003 could generate sales of $1 billion to $2 billion annually if it succeeds.

"The acquisition aligns with Eli Lilly's expanding neuroscience portfolio and offers upside potential in large markets like depression."

— Emily Field, Barclays analyst

Trump Administration Opens the Door

The deal taps into a regulatory environment that has become increasingly friendly to psychedelic research. In April, President Trump signed an executive directive to accelerate the FDA's review of psychedelic drugs for serious mental illnesses, a move that sent AtaiBeckley shares up 22% in a single day.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a longtime advocate for psychedelic therapies, lending political momentum to a field that was considered fringe just a few years ago.

The broader psychedelic therapeutics market is growing rapidly. RBC Capital Markets analyst Trung Huynh estimates the industry could reach $12 billion in revenue by 2034, rivaling the $8 billion branded antidepressant market today. Compass Pathways is nearing potential approval for a psilocybin-based treatment, and Definium Therapeutics recently reported positive results for an LSD-based drug in major depressive disorder.

A Peculiar Origin Story

AtaiBeckley itself has an unusual pedigree. The company was formed a year ago through the $390 million merger of Atai Life Sciences and Beckley Psytech. Beckley Psytech was spun out of the Beckley Foundation, an institute founded in 1998 by the late Amanda Feilding, Countess of Wemyss and March, at her Tudor hunting lodge near Oxford, England. Early investors included billionaire Jim Mellon and Innocent Drinks co-founder Richard Reed.

The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026.
